name: Acqua Panna
comment: NO₃ 2.1 mg/L (reported as 0.48 mg/L nitrate-as-N). HCO₃ derived from total alkalinity 90 mg/L as CaCO₃. K below detection limit. Still water (no CO₂).
description: Still natural mineral water from the Panna spring in the Tuscan Apennines near Florence, with a light overall mineral content.

provenance.source: Acqua Panna Water Analysis Report 2023 (Sanpellegrino S.p.A.); Panna Spring, Scarperia (Florence), Italy

name: Antipodes
comment: Used for strong, pale, bitter ales. SiO₂ 73 mg/L (dominant mineral). Silica-rich artesian water, Whakatāne, NZ; total minerality ~130 mg/L. Bottler states analysis accurate to ±20%.
description: Artesian water from Whakatāne on New Zealand's North Island, notable for a high dissolved-silica content.

provenance.source: Antipodes official typical analysis (antipodes.co.nz; full ion set via Fonsapor distributor reproduction)

name: Apollinaris
comment: Used for dark, soft flavored beers. Apollinaris (Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler, Coca-Cola) — Apollinaris Classic/Selection mineralisation. Classic/Medium were withdrawn from German retail; Selection remains (gastronomy/export), same source water.
description: Heavily mineralised sodium-bicarbonate water from Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler in the German Ahr valley.

provenance.source: Apollinaris official mineralisation (Apollinaris Classic/Selection, Coca-Cola DE)

name: Aquarel Birken
comment: Used for dark, soft flavored beers. HISTORICAL / unverified-current: Nestlé Aquarel (Birken Quelle, Naturell) is no longer marketed in Germany — no current bottler source. Values from mineralwasser-test.com label transcription. Removal-sub-issue candidate.
description: A formerly marketed German bottled water (Birken Quelle); the brand is no longer sold and the figures come from a historical label transcription.

provenance.source: mineralwasser-test.com label transcription (Nestlé Aquarel Birken Quelle Naturell) — brand discontinued in DE, no current source

name: Artificial mineral water
comment: Synthetic recipe: Ca:Mg 1:1, Na ≈ 125 mg/L, per Kulhavý & Čuta (Vodní Hospodářství B, 1973). The 1973 paper could not be located online; only the Na optimum is independently corroborated (Marcussen et al. 2020). HCO₃/SO₄/Cl values unverified against a primary source.
description: A constructed reference recipe balancing calcium and magnesium with moderate sodium, drawn from a mid-century study on mineral content in water; not a bottled product.

provenance.source: Kulhavý & Čuta, Vodní Hospodářství B 1973, 23(9), 222–6 'Effects of mineral content on the taste of water' (primary not located online); Na≈125 mg/L optimum corroborated by Marcussen et al., Foods 2020, 9(12), 1875.

name: Badoit

provenance.source: Estimate. No producer-published bottled-carbonation spec found (badoit.fr composition page lists no CO₂/volumes figure). Badoit is consistently classified as LIGHT carbonation — below San Pellegrino and well below Perrier (~5 vol) — per the Sparkel 'Science of Carbonation' comparison (qualitative chart, no number). ~1.5 volumes (≈2.9 g/L) reflects that light position. NOT derived from source-CO₂: the widely-cited '~3 g/L' number is a historical 1856 spring analysis (source dissolved CO₂), not a bottled spec, and is not used here as a target. Replace with an authoritative figure if one is published.

comment: Naturally carbonated. SiO₂ 27 mg/L, F⁻ 1.2 mg/L. Official badoit.fr table omits K, pH, TDS and CO₂; prior Khymos-2015 values for those fields dropped.
description: Naturally carbonated mineral water from Saint-Galmier in the French Loire department, with substantial sodium, magnesium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Badoit official composition page (badoit.fr — Tableau de composition, valeurs moyennes pour 1 litre)

name: Borsec
comment: Naturally carbonated (Romaqua Group). CO₂ is the label minimum (≥2500 mg/L); TDS is dry residue at 180°C. K, SO₄ and Cl were Khymos-origin and are not on the current product label, so they were dropped.
description: Naturally carbonated mineral water from the Borsec resort in the Romanian Eastern Carpathians, rich in calcium, magnesium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Romaqua Group — Borsec natural carbonated mineral water product label / analysis (Ca 364.3, Mg 110.5, Na 78.33, HCO₃ 1962.8 mg/L, pH 5.75, CO₂ ≥2500 mg/L, dry residue 1490 mg/L)

name: Burton (beer brewing)
comment: NO₃ 31 mg/L. HCO₃ corrected from Khymos 141 to 320 mg/L per John Palmer 'How to Brew' Table 21 (Burton-on-Trent IPA profile). Ca/Mg/SO4 retain Khymos values; historical well analyses vary widely.
description: A brewing-water reference modelled on the high-sulfate well water of Burton-on-Trent, historically associated with English pale ales.

provenance.source: John Palmer — How to Brew (4th ed.), Table 21 (Burton-on-Trent IPA water)

name: Buxton
comment: Still natural mineral water, St Ann's spring (Buxton, Derbyshire, UK; Nestlé Waters). Still and sparkling share this analysis, differing only in carbonation (sparkling pH ~5.2). NO₃ <0.1 mg/L. TDS is dry residue at 180°C; no F or SiO₂ published.
description: Still natural mineral water from St Ann's spring at Buxton in the English Peak District.

provenance.source: Buxton Water (Nestlé Waters UK) — 'Bottled Water Nutritional Information' typical analysis; corroborated by the printed product label (Open Food Facts EAN 5015552555132: Ca 55, Mg 19, K 1, Cl 37 mg/L)

name: Calistoga Spring Water
comment: Still Spring Water line; springs: Lukens Spring (Baxter, CA) and/or Sopiago Spring (El Dorado County, CA). Source reports alkalinity as CaCO₃ (40 mg/L as CaCO₃; not pre-converted). Cl and NO₃-as-N reported non-detect (Cl omitted). Low-mineral spring water.
description: A low-mineral spring water bottled in California, drawn from springs in the Sierra Nevada foothills.

provenance.source: 2021 Calistoga Water Analysis Report, ©2021 BlueTriton Brands, Inc. — Calistoga® Spring Water column (Secondary Inorganics: Ca 8, Mg 2.9, Na 3.7, K 1.5, Alkalinity Total as CaCO₃ 40, SO₄ 0.62, Cl ND, pH 7.5, TDS 78)

name: Carola Rouge
comment: NO₃ 1.5 mg/L. Carbonation grade only (Rouge); ion composition is shared across Carola variants. Now classified as eau de source.
description: Carbonated spring water from Ribeauvillé in Alsace; the Rouge grade denotes the carbonation level among the Carola variants.

provenance.source: Carola Rouge product label (Sources Alma) as transcribed on Open Food Facts; matches carola.fr composition cited by fr.wikipedia

name: Contrex
comment: NO₃ 2.9 mg/L. Still water. Major ions and TDS 2078 confirmed against current Contrex/Nestlé label.
description: Still mineral water from Contrexéville in the Vosges, with very high calcium and sulfate content.

provenance.source: Contrex official composition (contrex.fr / Nestlé), label transcription via Open Food Facts EAN 7613035866386

name: Dorna
comment: Dorna natural carbonated mineral water (Poiana Vinului source). NO₃ 0.26 mg/L; Cl <5 mg/L (omitted). TDS is dry residue at 180°C. The current bottler declaration publishes a real HCO₃ (680.8 mg/L), so the prior Khymos HCO₃=0 placeholder, plus the Khymos-origin K, SO₄, Cl and CO₂ figures (not on the current declaration), were dropped.
description: Naturally carbonated mineral water from the Poiana Vinului source in the Romanian Carpathians, dominated by calcium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: The Coca-Cola Company (Romania) — Dorna natural carbonated mineral water nutritional declaration, Poiana Vinului source (Ca 211.1, Mg 14.6, Na 10.25, HCO₃ 680.8 mg/L, NO₃ 0.26, Cl <5, pH 5.88, dry residue 644 mg/L)

name: Evian
comment: NO₃ 3.8 mg/L.
description: Still mineral water from Évian-les-Bains on the French shore of Lake Geneva, with moderate calcium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Evian official water quality page (evian.com/en_int)

name: Farris
comment: Carbonated; Si 6 mg/L. Total mineral content ~1400 mg/L. High Na/Cl gives a large charge-balance residual (KNOWN_IMBALANCED). pH not published by the bottler.
description: Carbonated mineral water from Larvik in Norway, with high sodium and chloride content.

provenance.source: Ringnes AS official Farris naturell product analysis (ringnes.no)

name: Ferrarelle
comment: Naturally sparkling ("effervescente naturale"), Ferrarelle spring, Riardo (Caserta, Campania, Italy). CO₂ is the free-CO₂-at-source figure from the official EPD. NO₃ 3.5 mg/L, F 1.0 mg/L, SiO₂ 84 mg/L. TDS is dry residue at 180°C.
description: Naturally sparkling mineral water from the Ferrarelle spring at Riardo in Campania, high in calcium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Ferrarelle S.p.A. — official Bottled Water Report, Ferrarelle Sparkling (report date 2024-05-20); SiO₂ (84) and free CO₂ at source (2600) from the official Ferrarelle Environmental Product Declaration 'The Composition' table

name: Fiji
comment: Silica-rich artesian water, Yaqara Valley aquifer, Viti Levu, Fiji. SiO₂ 93 mg/L (dominant mineral; fills the high-silica chemistry gap). F 0.24 mg/L, NO₃ ~0.27 mg/L. Core ions from the bottler's 'Typical Analysis'; SO₄ and NO₃ are from the FineWaters profile (not in the bottler table) and are lower-confidence.
description: Artesian water from the Yaqara Valley aquifer on Viti Levu, Fiji, notable for its high dissolved silica.

provenance.source: FIJI Water official FAQ — 'Typical Analysis in Milligrams per Liter' (Na 18, K 4.9, Ca 18, Mg 15, Cl 9.3, HCO₃ 152, SiO₂ 93, F 0.24, TDS 222, pH 7.7); corroborated by the FIJI Water Company quality report

name: Fiuggi
comment: NO₃ 3.1 mg/L. SiO₂ ~16–33 mg/L. Cl not published on current analysis (Khymos value dropped). Fonte Fiuggi (FR), Lazio.
description: Still low-mineral water from the Fonte Fiuggi spring in Lazio, central Italy.

provenance.source: Acqua Fiuggi label — chemical-physical analysis, Università di Roma "La Sapienza" (SO₄/NO₃ from acquafiuggi.com-cited label); transcribed by Beverfood

name: Gerolsteiner

provenance.source: Gerolsteiner official product page: "Gerolsteiner Sprudel enthält 7 g Kohlensäure pro Liter" — exclusively natural carbonation, bottled to match the source. Producer-stated bottled carbonation, independently published from (not derived from) the analysis-sheet source-CO₂ figure.

comment: NO₃ 5.1 mg/L.
description: Naturally carbonated mineral water from Gerolstein in the German Eifel, high in calcium, magnesium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Gerolsteiner official analysis sheet 2024 (Analyseblatt Sprudel International)

name: Hassia Sprudel
comment: Hassia Sprudel (Bad Vilbel) — official Hassia mineralisation (SGS Institut Fresenius).
description: Carbonated mineral water from Bad Vilbel near Frankfurt, with high calcium, sodium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Hassia official product page — Hassia Sprudel mineralisation (SGS Institut Fresenius)

name: Henniez
comment: NO₃ 14 mg/L. TDS is total mineralisation (571 mg/L) from the bottler.
description: Mineral water from Henniez in the Swiss canton of Vaud, dominated by calcium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Henniez official characteristic-components analysis (henniez.ch, source de vie)

name: Hépar
comment: Still water, Vittel (Vosges, France; Nestlé Waters). The most magnesium-rich still natural mineral water on the French market (Mg 119 mg/L) and very high sulfate (SO₄ 1530 mg/L) — fills the high-Mg / high-SO₄ chemistry gap. NO₃ 4.3 mg/L, F 0.4 mg/L. TDS is dry residue at 180°C; no CaCO₃ alkalinity or SiO₂ published.
description: Still mineral water from Vittel in the Vosges, exceptionally high in magnesium and sulfate.

provenance.source: Nestlé Waters Marketing & Distribution (bottler of Hépar®) — 'Tableau des teneurs en minéraux des eaux minérales naturelles', row HÉPAR, June 2024 (values read from commercial labels); cross-confirmed by hepar.fr (Mg 119, Na 14.2) and the bottle label (OFF EAN 7613035024021)

name: Highland Spring
comment: Still spring water, Blackford (Ochil Hills, Perthshire, UK). NO₃ 3.1 mg/L. Still and sparkling share this 'average analysis at source'; sparkling differs only in carbonation (pH ~4–5). TDS is dry residue at 180°C; no F or SiO₂ published by the bottler.
description: Still spring water from Blackford in the Ochil Hills of Perthshire, Scotland, with a modest mineral content.

provenance.source: Highland Spring — 'Spring Water' product page 'Average Analysis at source' table (mg/L); identical table on the 'Sparkling Water' page; pH from the 'Our Water' page (highlandspring.com)

name: London (beer brewing)
comment: NO₃ 3 mg/L. HCO₃ corrected from Khymos 123 to 104 mg/L per John Palmer 'How to Brew' Table 21 (London Bitter profile). Ca/Mg/Na/SO4/Cl retain Khymos values; historical well analyses vary widely. Classic recipe; NO₃ unmeasured/excluded and knowingly charge-imbalanced.
description: A brewing-water reference modelled on London's historical supply, associated with English bitters and dark ales.

provenance.source: John Palmer — How to Brew (4th ed.), Table 21 (London Bitter water)

name: Magnetic Springs
comment: Magnetic Springs Spring water (still), sourced from Pine Grove Springs, Columbus, Ohio — a low-mineralisation US spring. SiO₂ 9.6 mg/L. NO₃ as N 0.78 mg/L (≈ NO₃ 3.5 mg/L). Sulfate below the lab reporting limit (<5 mg/L, treated as absent). Alkalinity reported as CaCO₃ (40 mg/L).
description: Low-mineral spring water drawn from Pine Grove Springs and bottled in Columbus, Ohio.

provenance.source: Magnetic Springs Water Co. — Spring Water Annual Testing report (National Testing Laboratories, NELAP-accredited; sample 439363, collected 2022-12-30)

name: Mountain Valley Spring
comment: The Mountain Valley® Spring Water (still), Ouachita Mountains, AR. NO₃ as N: ND. Ion values are midpoints of the reported ranges from the 2025 Water Analysis Report (Ca 65–70, Mg 6.1–7.2, Na 1.7–2.5, K ND–1.2, Cl 1.8–2.5, SO₄ 5.2–8.2, pH 7.3–8.1). Alkalinity reported as CaCO₃ (190 mg/L).
description: Still spring water from the Ouachita Mountains of Arkansas, with moderate calcium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Mountain Valley Spring Water — 2025 Water Analysis Report (The Mountain Valley® Spring Water column)

name: Munich (beer brewing)
comment: NO₃ 3 mg/L. HCO₃ corrected from Khymos 164 to 152 mg/L per John Palmer 'How to Brew' Table 21 (Munich Oktoberfest profile). Ca/Mg/Na/SO4/Cl retain Khymos values (Ca/Mg closely match Palmer); historical well analyses vary widely. Classic recipe; NO₃ unmeasured/excluded and knowingly charge-imbalanced.
description: A brewing-water reference modelled on Munich's water, associated with malty German lagers.

provenance.source: John Palmer — How to Brew (4th ed.), Table 21 (Munich Oktoberfest water)

name: Neuselters
comment: HISTORICAL / unverified-current: Neuselters Mineralquellen (Löhnberg) permanently closed Feb 2016 — no current authoritative source exists. Values from mineralwasser-test.com label transcription (Neuselters Still). Removal-sub-issue candidate.
description: A formerly marketed German mineral water from Löhnberg; the source closed in 2016 and the figures come from a historical label transcription.

provenance.source: mineralwasser-test.com label transcription (Neuselters Still) — brand discontinued 2016, no current source

name: Perla Harghitei
comment: Naturally carbonated flagship ("Carbo"), Sâncrăieni source. CO₂ is the label minimum (≥3500 mg/L). The lightly-carbonated "Ușor Carbo" variant shares this analysis, differing only in CO₂. No NO₃, F, or SiO₂ published.
description: Naturally carbonated mineral water from the Sâncrăieni source in Romania's Harghita county, rich in calcium, magnesium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: S.C. Perla Harghitei S.A. — "Perla Harghitei" (Carbo) product page, published mineral-water analysis (Sâncrăieni, Harghita), perlaharghitei.ro

name: Perla Harghitei Plată
comment: Still ("Plată") line — chemically distinct from the carbonated Perla Harghitei, drawn from a different spring (FH Artezia 2, Sânsimion): much lower Mg/Na/HCO₃. No NO₃, F, or SiO₂ published.
description: Still mineral water from the Sânsimion source in Harghita county, Romania, drawn from a different spring than the carbonated Perla Harghitei.

provenance.source: S.C. Perla Harghitei S.A. — "Perla Harghitei" (Plată) product page, published mineral-water analysis (FH Artezia 2, Sânsimion), perlaharghitei.ro

name: Perrier

provenance.source: Estimate. No producer-published bottled-carbonation spec found; ~5.0 volumes is the figure widely cited for Perrier across secondary industry/hobbyist sources (e.g. Sparkel 'The Science of Carbonation', CySoda). NOT derived from the source-CO₂ value. Replace with an authoritative figure if one is published.

comment: NO₃ 7.3 mg/L. Current product label (Vergèze). Nestlé's corporate fact sheet differs (Ca 155, Mg 6.8, SO₄ 33, Cl 22, HCO₃ 430) — Perrier's published composition varies by source/period. carbonation_target ≈5.0 volumes is an unverified estimate (see carbonation_target.provenance), not a producer spec.
description: Naturally carbonated mineral water from Vergèze in southern France, with high calcium and bicarbonate.

name: Pilsen (beer brewing)

description: A brewing-water reference modelled on the very soft water of Plzeň, associated with pale Czech pilsners.

provenance.source: John Palmer — How to Brew (4th ed.), Table 21 (Pilsen Pilsner water)

name: PurPur (coffee brewing)
comment: Provenance unrecoverable: no primary reference ties this 'PurPur' composition to a documented coffee-water recipe. Values retained from the Khymos v6 calculator pending a credible source.
description: A coffee-brewing water target of uncertain origin, retained from an upstream calculator pending a verifiable source.

name: Rosbacher Klassich

provenance.source: Rosbacher official mineralisation — Rosbacher Klassisch (Institut Fresenius, Taunusstein)

name: Saint-Yorre
comment: Naturally carbonated (Source Royale). F⁻ < 1.5 mg/L. Very high mineralisation; known charge-imbalanced.
description: Naturally carbonated mineral water from Saint-Yorre in the French Allier, very high in sodium and bicarbonate.

provenance.source: Saint-Yorre official composition (st-yorre.com — Source Royale, composition moyenne en mg/l)

name: Salvus

description: Mineral water from Emsdetten in north-west Germany, with notable calcium, sulfate and chloride.

provenance.source: Salvus official mineralisation — Salvus Classic (Institut Romeis)

name: San Benedetto
comment: NO₃ 9 mg/L. SiO₂ 16.6 mg/L. Fonte San Benedetto, Scorzè (VE). Still water.
description: Still mineral water from the Fonte San Benedetto at Scorzè in the Veneto, with moderate mineralisation.

provenance.source: San Benedetto official scheda tecnica (Acqua Minerale San Benedetto S.p.A.), analysis Università di Napoli Federico II 04/07/2019

name: San Narciso
comment: F⁻ 2.3 mg/L. TDS = dry residue at 180 °C. Naturally carbonated bicarbonate-sodium water (Caldes de Malavella). Bottler confirms "agua con gas natural" (natural volcanic CO₂) but publishes no numeric CO₂ figure, so co2 is left unset. Published ion set shows an anion excess (known imbalanced). Prior 2015 "little gas" ambiguity resolved.
description: Naturally carbonated sodium-bicarbonate water from Caldes de Malavella in Catalonia, drawn from a volcanic-CO₂ spring.

provenance.source: San Narciso official mineral analysis (sannarciso.com)

name: San Pellegrino

provenance.source: Estimate. S.Pellegrino is force-carbonated ("acqua naturale con aggiunta di anidride carbonica"); no producer-published finished-product carbonation spec in g/L or volumes was found, including in the official S.Pellegrino Water Analysis Report. ~3.0 volumes is the figure independent secondary carbonation-testing sources converge on (Billi UK ≈ 13 PSI at 35°F reported as a 3.00:1 rating; corroborated by Sparkel/Bonne O as moderate carbonation). NOT derived from source CO₂ (this profile records no co2). Replace with an authoritative figure if the producer publishes one.

comment: NO₃ 2.9 mg/L. pH 5.7 as sold (7.6 at source). Previous 2015 Khymos values ran ~14–32% high.
description: Carbonated mineral water from San Pellegrino Terme in Lombardy, high in calcium and sulfate.

provenance.source: S.Pellegrino Water Analysis Report 2021 (via Wikipedia / S.Pellegrino US)

name: SCA target (coffee brewing)
comment: NO₃ 0 mg/L. Target derived from the SCA (formerly SCAA) 'Water for Brewing Specialty Coffee' standard, which specifies Calcium Hardness 68 mg/L and Total Alkalinity 40 mg/L expressed as CaCO₃. Converted to elemental Ca ≈ 27 mg/L and HCO₃ ≈ 49 mg/L. Corrected from the prior Khymos encoding (Ca 68, HCO₃ 233) which read the CaCO₃ hardness figure as elemental Ca.
description: A coffee-brewing water target derived from the Specialty Coffee Association's recommended calcium hardness and alkalinity standard.

provenance.source: Specialty Coffee Association (formerly SCAA) — Water for Brewing Specialty Coffee standard (rev. 21 Nov 2009)

name: Selters
comment: Original Selters Classic (Löhnberg-Selters) — official mineralisation, SGS Institut Fresenius analysis 2014-03-13. CO₂ figure not published by bottler; Khymos-era value dropped.
description: Mineral water from Löhnberg-Selters in Hesse, with high sodium, bicarbonate and chloride; the original Selters spring.

provenance.source: Original Selters official mineralisation — Selters Classic (SGS Institut Fresenius, 2014-03-13)

name: Tea brewing (max)

name: Tea brewing (min)

provenance.source: US Patent Application 2006/0286263 A1 (Conopco/Unilever), "Functional water 1" (Table I)

name: Ty Nant

name: Vichy Catalan
comment: High-sodium naturally carbonated Na-HCO₃ water, Caldes de Malavella (Girona, Spain); hyperthermal spring (~60 °C at source). Li 1.7, NO₃ 1.1, SiO₂ ~58 mg/L. name: Vichy Célestins

description: Naturally sparkling sodium-bicarbonate water from Vichy in the French Allier, very high in sodium and bicarbonate.

name: Waiākea
comment: Waiākea® Hawaiian Volcanic Water, a naturally alkaline deep-well water from the Keaʻau aquifer at the eastern base of Mauna Loa, Hilo, Hawaiʻi. SiO₂ 37 mg/L (silica-rich volcanic water). F 0.061 mg/L. NO₃ as N: ND. Alkalinity reported as CaCO₃ (31 mg/L). Note: the bottler's 2026 General Mineral Analysis prints Fluoride 2.9 / Magnesium 0.061; these are transposed — the same report's Product Analysis table independently reports Fluoride 0.061, so the corrected values are F 0.061 / Mg 2.9 (also consistent with prior typical analyses and charge balance).
description: Naturally alkaline deep-well water filtered through volcanic rock at the base of Mauna Loa on Hawaii, with notable silica.

provenance.source: Waiākea Hawaiian Volcanic — Bottled Water Quality Report 2026 (Typical Mineral Analysis, sampling period March 2026)
